articles.title: MLB stands by warning to players over Pride Night protest but faults Giants for poor communication
articles.summary: In a letter to Sen. Josh Hawley, Major League Baseball denied it targeted players who oppose gay rights and partially blamed the San Francisco Giants for the team’s Pride Night fiasco.
articles.body: Major League Baseball denied that it targeted players who oppose gay rights and put some of the blame on the San Francisco Giants for an embarrassing flap at the team’s Pride Night celebration, a letter from Commissioner Rob Manfred revealed Monday. Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., posted the letter, in which Manfred defended MLB against allegations that it was forcing players to celebrate the LGBTQ+ community. The Giants held their annual Pride Night on June 12 at Oracle Park, with most players wearing caps that had the team’s iconic interlocking “SF” logo in rainbow colors, instead of its traditional orange and black. But three Giants that night — pitcher Landen Roupp and relievers JT Brubaker and Ryan Walker — scrawled a Bible verse, “Gen 9:12-16,” on their caps. Some opponents of gay rights have used Genesis 9:12-16 as their rallying call. Following the silent protest, MLB warned players not to deface their uniforms. “MLB’s policy must be uniformly enforced regardless of the message in order for it to survive legal challenge, which means prohibiting both the positive message and the negative message,” Manfred wrote in his letter to Hawley. “By warning the Giants players that they may not include Bible verses on their caps in the future, MLB was not discriminating or chastising those players based on their religious beliefs; rather MLB was enforcing (with only an oral warning) a long-standing, collectively bargained rule that keeps uniforms clean and avoids controversy.” “The rule has been similarly applied to a variety of messages, some as innocuous as messages to a player’s mother or honoring a deceased friend,” he wrote. In posting the letter from Manfred, Hawley claimed victory over Major League Baseball, saying Manfred “admitted” fault in the office’s handling of the Giants’ Pride Night. “Commissioner writes to me and admits they were wrong to threaten the Giants players over Bible verses and promises never to fine or discipline these players — or any players for their religious beliefs,” Hawley said in a statement Monday releasing the letter. But in the 1,039-word letter from MLB to Hawley, Manfred never uses the word “wrong” or admits any MLB-issued threat of fines or discipline. An MLB representative declined to comment Tuesday on Hawley’s characterization of Manfred’s letter. Manfred seemed to blame the flap on the Giants, saying the club failed to properly inform players they didn’t need to wear the Pride Night rainbow cap. All 26 players could have opted to wear their normal uniforms, as Giants reliever Sam Hentges opted to do, MLB said. “Unfortunately, this year the Giants communication with players was inadequate and not clear. Some players apparently did not understand that they had the option to wear their normal uniform and elected to add messages to their hats bearing the pride logo as a result,” Manfred wrote. “The Giants players were allowed to wear the hats with the biblical references for the entire game. After the game had concluded, my office issued a routine oral warning about the uniform policy violation — unfortunately it was issued before we became aware of the Giants’ lapse in communication. The players were neither fined nor disciplined, nor will they ever be.” San Francisco has long been a focal point of gay culture in America, with about 16% of the city identifying as LGBTQ+. In a meeting with reporters Tuesday, Buster Posey, the Giants president of baseball operations, declined to address the Pride Night dispute or the commissioner’s criticism of the team. “I understand that there’s strong feelings on this topic,” said Posey, the team’s iconic catcher who led San Francisco to three World Series titles in the 2010s. “There’s differing perspectives, and out of respect to everybody involved, it’s not something that I’m going to revisit.” He was asked multiple questions about the June 12 incident and whether he ever objected to Pride Night as a player. “I’ll answer baseball questions,” Posey repeatedly said. The Giants pitchers’ quiet protest might have inspired players of the minor-league York Revolution last week to refuse to wear uniforms that had rainbow sleeves. Fewer than nine players agreed to wear the commemorative jerseys, and the Revolution forfeited the game, team officials said.

articles.title: Tens of thousands march in the first Budapest Pride since Viktor Orbán was voted out
articles.summary: The march began Saturday afternoon as temperatures reached at least 100 degrees amid a record heat wave that has gripped most of Europe.
articles.body: BUDAPEST, Hungary — Tens of thousands of people gathered in soaring temperatures in Hungary’s capital on Saturday to celebrate the 31st annual Budapest Pride, the first such LGBTQ+ march since former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who had sought to ban the event, was ousted in an April election. The march began Saturday afternoon as temperatures reached at least 100 degrees amid a record-breaking heat wave that has gripped most of Europe. Organizers distributed water bottles to marchers, and the city’s public water utility opened fountains along the route. Participants set off from Budapest’s iconic Opera House and wound through the city center before crossing the Erzsébet Bridge over the Danube River. Members of Hungary’s LGBTQ+ community and masses of supporters danced to music and waved rainbow flags. Luca Új, who was participating in her third Pride event, said she felt the mood at the march was more relaxed now that Orbán’s government, which implemented numerous anti-LGBTQ+ policies during its 16 years in power, had been defeated. “There used to be a lot of tension. But now I see people as being somehow happier, and there are more older people, too,” she said. Saturday’s Pride march came a little more than a year after Orbán’s nationalist-populist government passed legislation and a constitutional amendment to outlaw the event, drawing criticism from human rights groups and politicians across the European Union. Yet in open defiance of the ban, last year’s Pride went on as planned and was the biggest in Hungary’s history, with organizers estimating attendance at over 350,000. The massive turnout for the march, which the government for months had insisted would no longer be permitted, was seen as a major blow to Orbán’s prestige. Orbán was handily defeated in the April election by a center-right challenger, Prime Minister Péter Magyar and his Tisza party. Hungary’s new government has not repealed the Orbán-era legislation that outlawed Pride, but police this year authorized the event and were providing security along the route. Kristóf Györgyi, a first-time Pride participant who traveled to Budapest from the southern city of Szeged, said he has high hopes that Hungary’s new government will take steps to extend rights to sexual minorities that are available in many other European countries. “The fact that there’s already a debate in Parliament about whether an orphaned child is better off with a same-sex couple or in an orphanage is a positive sign,” he said, referring to the Orbán-era ban on same-sex adoption, as well as same-sex marriage. “Obviously, the laws haven’t changed yet, but there are already many signs of hope for our community,” he said. Hungary’s previous government long insisted that Pride, a celebration of LGBTQ+ visibility and struggle for equal rights, was a violation of children’s rights to moral and spiritual development — something rights groups and many experts have rejected. In April, the E.U.’s highest court ruled that Orbán-era legislation from 2021 that banned the availability of LGBTQ+ content to minors violates E.U. law and breaches a foundational treaty guaranteeing respect for human rights and equality.

Luca Új, who was participating in her third Pride event, said she felt the mood at the march was more relaxed now that Orbán’s government, which implemented numerous anti-LGBTQ+ policies during its 16 years in power, had been defeated. “There used to be a lot of tension. But now I see people as being somehow happier, and there are more older people, too,” she said. Saturday’s Pride march came a little more than a year after Orbán’s nationalist-populist government passed legislation and a constitutional amendment to outlaw the event, drawing criticism from human rights groups and politicians across the European Union. Yet in open defiance of the ban, last year’s Pride went on as planned and was the biggest in Hungary’s history, with organizers estimating attendance at over 350,000. The massive turnout for the march, which the government for months had insisted would no longer be permitted, was seen as a major blow to Orbán’s prestige. Orbán was handily defeated in the April election by a center-right challenger, Prime Minister Péter Magyar and his Tisza party. Hungary’s new government has not repealed the Orbán-era legislation that outlawed Pride, but police this year authorized the event and were providing security along the route. Kristóf Györgyi, a first-time Pride participant who traveled to Budapest from the southern city of Szeged, said he has high hopes that Hungary’s new government will take steps to extend rights to sexual minorities that are available in many other European countries. “The fact that there’s already a debate in Parliament about whether an orphaned child is better off with a same-sex couple or in an orphanage is a positive sign,” he said, referring to the Orbán-era ban on same-sex adoption, as well as same-sex marriage. “Obviously, the laws haven’t changed yet, but there are already many signs of hope for our community,” he said. Hungary’s previous government long insisted that Pride, a celebration of LGBTQ+ visibility and struggle for equal rights, was a violation of children’s rights to moral and spiritual development — something rights groups and many experts have rejected. In April, the E.U.’s highest court ruled that Orbán-era legislation from 2021 that banned the availability of LGBTQ+ content to minors violates E.U. law and breaches a foundational treaty guaranteeing respect for human rights and equality.

articles.title: California gets Bruce Lee Day in a first for US state’s Chinese Americans
articles.summary: Bruce Lee Day aims to honour the San Francisco-born martial arts legend as a cultural bridge and Asian-American icon.
articles.body:
Martial arts icon Bruce Lee will become the first Chinese American in California history to be honoured with an annual namesake day.

California Governor Gavin Newsom signed a law on Tuesday afternoon, officially designating May 17 as Bruce Lee Day.

list 1 of 4 At least 22 killed in Kyiv as Zelenskyy warns of ‘massive Russian strike’

list 2 of 4 EU border rules causing travel chaos ahead of summer peak, industry warns

list 3 of 4 German prosecutors charge Ukrainian suspect over Nord Stream explosions

list 4 of 4 US designates Ecuador’s Chone Killers gang as ‘terrorist’ organisation

Lee was born in San Francisco in 1940 and returned to the city on May 17, 1959, aged 18, after spending his childhood in Hong Kong.

His daughter, Shannon Lee, CEO of the Bruce Lee Foundation, said the honour reflects her father’s enduring legacy as a bridge between cultures.

“From young people who found confidence and possibility in his philosophy, to families who finally saw themselves represented on screen, to athletes who still draw on his teachings of discipline and inner strength, his reach is profound,” she said in a statement.

State Assembly member Matt Haney, who represents San Francisco, called Lee the “epitome of the best of California”.

“At a time when Asian Americans were too often absent from or stereotyped on screen, Bruce Lee helped generations see themselves represented with strength and dignity,” he said.

The Bruce Lee Foundation and Asian-American groups hope Bruce Lee will be celebrated each year with voluntary activities, including cultural exhibits, public events and classroom lessons.

Born to Chinese parents touring the US with an opera, Lee held birthright citizenship. He moved to Hong Kong as an infant, became a child actor, and studied Chinese kung fu before returning to the US in 1959.

He enrolled at the University of Washington in Seattle in 1961, but dropped out to teach martial arts.

In the 1960s, Lee appeared in Hollywood, most notably as Kato in the TV series The Green Hornet, but said studios typecast him in racist roles and paid him less than white actors.

He returned to Hong Kong and starred in martial arts films, including The Big Boss and Fist of Fury.

Lee died tragically in 1973 at the age of 32 after an allergic reaction to pain medication.

His name and likeness remain widely popular.

Fans gather on his birthday, and a treatment he wrote for a television series inspired the HBO Max show “Warrior”.

articles.title: George E. Johnson, founder of pioneering Black hair products company, dies at 99
articles.summary: Johnson Products Co. was founded in 1954, catering to African Americans’ evolving tastes in hairstyles and ​fashion, in an era when U.S. companies paid little attention to Black consumers.
articles.body: George E. Johnson, the pioneering Chicago entrepreneur whose eponymous company transformed Black hair care in the United States with brands ​including Afro Sheen, Ultra Wave and Classy Curl, died on Monday at age 99, according to a family statement. The family said Johnson “passed away peacefully at home at the age of 99, leaving behind an extraordinary legacy of entrepreneurship, faith, perseverance, philanthropy, and family.” The New York Times, citing his second wife, Madeline Murphy Rabb, reported that ​Johnson died of a respiratory illness. Johnson Products Co. was founded in 1954, catering to African Americans’ evolving tastes in hairstyles, ​fashion and cosmetics in an era when U.S. companies and advertisers paid little attention to Black consumers. “He truly believed business could be a force for good, creating opportunity, strengthening communities, opening doors for others, and demonstrating that success carries with it a responsibility to serve,” the family statement said. The ⁠business, which Johnson co-founded with his first wife, Joan Johnson, who died in 2019, grew to command nearly 80% of the ​Black hair care market by 1960, and in 1971 became the first Black-owned company listed on the American Stock Exchange, now known as NYSE American. With ​a marketing campaign echoing slogans and imagery of the era’s Black Pride and Black Power movements, the company became the exclusive sponsor of the television music show “Soul Train,” helping the Chicago-based weekly program grow from a local broadcast into a nationally syndicated hit. The company’s own business roots illustrated the difficulties ​minority entrepreneurs faced at the dawn of the civil rights movement. Johnson, who was born in a sharecropper’s shack in Mississippi in 1927, moved to Chicago with his mother at age 2. He later worked as a door-to-door cosmetics salesman after dropping out of ​high school and launched his own venture with a bank loan of just $250 he secured by telling a white loan officer he wanted to borrow ‌the money ⁠for a family vacation. “I knew this request (for a vacation loan) wouldn’t rattle [the loan officer’s] belief that he was superior to me. Nor would it challenge his stereotypes of Black men as subservient or unintelligent,” Johnson recounted in his 2025 memoir, “Afro ​Sheen.” Some ​of the company’s first major ⁠brands, including Ultra Wave for men and Ultra Sheen for women, were introduced as hair-relaxing products designed for home use, to achieve straight and wavy hairstyles popular in the 1950s and early 1960s. As Black Power ​consciousness gave rise to an increasing preference among Black people for a more natural hair texture and look ​that did not ⁠seek to mimic the styles worn by whites, Johnson’s company adapted with the advent of its Afro Sheen Blow Out kit in the late 1960s, according to BlackPast.org. The company’s Classy Curl helped consumers achieve the “Jheri curl” perm first popularized by white hairdresser-chemist Jheri Redding. Johnson’s venture began to struggle ⁠as it ​faced competition from large hair care and cosmetics companies such as Revlon that ​sought to grab market share in the increasingly lucrative African American hairstyling business. After the Johnsons divorced, ownership of their business changed hands a number of times before a majority African American investment ​firm acquired the business in 2009 from Procter & Gamble.

articles.title: How to buy a house: The ultimate guide for first-time home buyers
articles.summary: First-time home buyers often qualify for unique benefits. Learn what to expect as a first-time buyer when it comes to buying a house and getting a mortgage.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

As a first-time home buyer, you'll want to understand each step of the home-buying process, as well as your loan options and exclusive benefits. It's crucial to be prepared as you enter the housing market in 2026 for the first time.

To qualify for special home buyer benefits, borrowers purchasing a single-family home as a primary residence are defined as "first-time home buyers" in one of three ways:

You've never purchased a single-family home before.

You haven't owned a home in the last three years, including sole or joint ownership.

You're a displaced homemaker or single parent who has never owned a home other than jointly with a spouse in the last three years.

In addition, eligibility requirements for a first-time home buyer loan will typically include a steady household income and a manageable debt load. More on that later.

How buying your first home works: Step by step

As Step 1, you'll want to determine how much house you can afford comfortably . If you properly gauge your financial capacity, your monthly mortgage payment will feel right from the beginning and get even easier to make over time.

Divide your gross (pre-tax) monthly salary by four. That's a good start for a target monthly payment. But that's not just principal and interest payments. You will also want to include property taxes and homeowners insurance in the total.

Mortgage lenders often recommend that your housing costs total around 28% of your gross pay. That calculation is known as your debt-to-income ratio (DTI).

Don't forget to figure in closing costs. These costs include (but aren't limited to) things like your appraisal and home inspection fees, loan origination costs, and title insurance, and they generally cost between 2% and 5% of your home's purchase price. Here's an example:

Say you're buying a $500,000 home. Your closing costs will be 2% to 5% of the total, or between $10,000 and $25,000.

There are several ways to reduce your closing costs. You can often save thousands by simply comparing multiple lenders, looking for those offering lender credits, and negotiating directly with your lender.

In some markets, seller concessions may also help lower the cash required at closing.

Over the last 10-plus years, more than 60% of home buyers said they shopped more than one lender, according to Fannie Mae research. Gone are the days when buyers just went with a real estate agent's "preferred lender," no questions asked.

When comparing lenders, it's important to look beyond the advertised annual percentage rate (APR) for your preferred loan. You'll want to compare key criteria that impact your total loan experience.

For example, look at each company's mortgage origination fee. Search for lenders with low to no origination fees to help keep costs down.

Again, don't forget to consider the total closing costs. Comparing Loan Estimates from all lenders will help uncover costs beyond your monthly mortgage payment so you can find the lender with the lowest interest rate and total loan costs.

With at least one lender mortgage preapproval in hand, you can officially move on to what you've no doubt already been doing …

Now for the fun part: looking at houses.

Make a list of what you're looking for in a house, including the "must haves" and "would be nice to haves."

Attend open houses and scour the local market to find neighborhoods and amenities that suit you best. Find a couple of contenders: one to make an offer on and some backup options if your favorite falls through.

Your buyer's agent will handle the details of making an official offer and negotiating counteroffers. If you've come to terms with the seller, you'll likely have to put down some earnest money.

That money will be held until closing when you can usually apply it to your down payment or closing costs.

With a signed purchase agreement in hand, you can get real-deal loan offers. Each lender vying for your business will give you a written offer.

Ask each lender to provide you with a zero-discount-points offer. This way, you can compare apples to apples — and then decide if you want to buy mortgage discount points to lower your interest rate.

Once your offer is accepted and your loan is submitted to underwriting (the process that leads to loan approval/denial), you can move forward with the home appraisal, inspection, and other steps before closing.

One of those tasks will be shopping for homeowners' insurance. You know those "bundle and save" ads? Sure, shop your current vehicle insurance provider if you have one, but you can also move that policy to a new agent if you get a better package deal for your home and car policies. So, shop around like you did for a mortgage lender.

Three days before closing, you'll receive an official Closing Disclosure form detailing the mortgage interest and up-front fees you'll pay.

Then, on signing day, you close on the house.

As a first-time home buyer, you're entitled to some special benefits to help you make that leap from renting to owning.

Down payment and closing costs assistance

While 20% down has been the historical goal — because it eliminates private mortgage insurance, a fee to protect lenders from a default — first-time home buyers can make a minimum down payment of 3% of the home purchase price (and some lenders buy that down to 1%).

Another big benefit of being a first-timer: government and nonprofit first-time home-buyer programs that cover closing costs and down payment assistance. These loan programs empower potential homeowners from all walks of life: teachers, first responders, Native American borrowers, public housing residents, and low- and middle-income households.

While many programs involve loans or tax credits, you might also qualify for a first-time home buyer grant that you don't have to repay.

The Department of Housing and Urban Development offers resources for first-time home buyers to find assistance programs they may be eligible for. State housing finance agencies can also provide additional information on homeownership programs.

Some employers also offer homeownership assistance to help employees buy their first home. Ask your human resources rep if your company offers any such programs.

IIs a low credit score making it hard to qualify for a mortgage? Good news: the housing finance industry is expanding credit score qualifications.

The new credit scoring models span longer periods and consider rent payment history. It's an effort to "provide a more complete view of borrower creditworthiness," Fannie Mae said in an April press release.

Even so, the benchmarks lenders use for qualifying applicants for loans remain. With most lenders, first-time home buyers can get an FHA loan with a FICO credit score as low as 500 with 10% down, or a conventional loan with a score as low as 620.

To qualify for a more expensive home loan, called a jumbo mortgage, you'll likely need a FICO 700.

You need a score of 780 or higher to qualify for the most favorable interest rate on any product, according to a MyFICO analysis .

A good lender will walk you through all the types of mortgage programs you qualify for.

Home buyer education courses are also available to first-timers and can help you discover and understand the process for buying a house.

Mortgage rates are at their lowest point in over three years, but they can still be a sticking point for many first-time buyers. Current rates are just over 6%, but existing homeowners with rates of 5% or lower are unlikely to move and lose what is likely a significantly lower interest rate.

That's worsening the 3.8 million-unit housing supply shortage . As a result, Realtor.com estimates that a lack of affordable housing prevents 1.6 million Gen Z and millennial would-be buyers or renters from forming households.

Home prices have risen in the last few years, but they are beginning to moderate.

Finally, saving for a down payment stymies many first-time buyers. That can be blamed on recent high inflation, rising home prices, and lagging income growth.

Best types of mortgages for first-time home buyers

If this is your first time buying a home, consider one of the following types of home loans to finance your purchase:

FHA loans can be great for first-time buyers who may not have had time to pay down debts or build up credit yet. You only need a 580 credit score and 3.5% down payment (or a 500 credit score with 10% down). You can also have a DTI ratio of up to 43%.

VA loans are great choices for military personnel and their families. You don't need any down payment.

You might qualify for a USDA loan if you're a low- to moderate-income buyer in a rural area. USDA loans don't require down payments, either.

HomeReady (by Fannie Mae) and Home Possible (by Freddie Mac) are two mortgage programs that let you get a mortgage with just 3% down — and you may not need a minimum qualifying credit score.

How much do most first-time home buyers put down?

A 2025 report by the National Association of REALTORS® (NAR) stated that the typical down payment for first-time home buyers was 10% in 2025. This is much lower than that of repeat buyers, with a typical down payment of 23%, and 19% for all buyers.

What qualifies you as a first-time home buyer?

There are three ways to qualify as a first-time home buyer: You have never bought a single-family home before, you haven't owned a home in the last three years, or you're a displaced homemaker/single parent who hasn't owned a home in the last three years (unless it was joint ownership with a spouse).

Which loan is best for a first-time home buyer?

An FHA loan is the best option for many first-time buyers because it accepts lower credit scores and higher debt-to-income ratios (DTIs) than many other types of mortgages.

First-time home buyer benefits vary by lender. Some mortgage lenders offer down payment assistance programs available only to first-time buyers. Others allow for lower down payments on conventional loans — for example, a lender may require 5% down for repeat buyers but only 3% down for first-timers.

What are first-time buyer education courses?

Some mortgage programs require first-time home buyers to take an educational course so they're informed and prepared for homeownership. For example, HomeReady by Fannie Mae and Home Possible by Freddie Mac both require first-time buyers to complete online education courses.

Buying a house with a low income can be challenging, but it's possible with the right mortgage lender and program. Learn how to buy a home with a low income.

6 steps to choosing the right mortgage lender

Learn how to pick a home loan lender. To choose a mortgage lender, know which type of loan you want and what questions to ask, then apply for preapproval.

Having the right questions to ask your home loan lender can help you find the best mortgage terms for your financial situation.

The money needed for a down payment and closing costs can quickly add up. Learn how to save for a house by creating a savings goal, cutting expenses, and more.

Should you buy a house? How to know if you're ready.

When should you buy a house? The decision mostly comes down to your stage in life, credit score, and savings. Find out if you're ready to buy a home.

Want to buy a house before the end of 2026? Follow these crucial steps.

Do you want to buy a house this year? Learn what to expect from the 2026 housing market so you're prepared to buy.

HomeReady (by Fannie Mae) and Home Possible (by Freddie Mac) are two mortgage programs that let you get a mortgage with just 3% down — and you may not need a minimum qualifying credit score.
How much do most first-time home buyers put down?

A 2025 report by the National Association of REALTORS® (NAR) stated that the typical down payment for first-time home buyers was 10% in 2025. This is much lower than that of repeat buyers, with a typical down payment of 23%, and 19% for all buyers.
What qualifies you as a first-time home buyer?

There are three ways to qualify as a first-time home buyer: You have never bought a single-family home before, you haven't owned a home in the last three years, or you're a displaced homemaker/single parent who hasn't owned a home in the last three years (unless it was joint ownership with a spouse).
Which loan is best for a first-time home buyer?
An FHA loan is the best option for many first-time buyers because it accepts lower credit scores and higher debt-to-income ratios (DTIs) than many other types of mortgages.

First-time home buyer benefits vary by lender. Some mortgage lenders offer down payment assistance programs available only to first-time buyers. Others allow for lower down payments on conventional loans — for example, a lender may require 5% down for repeat buyers but only 3% down for first-timers.
What are first-time buyer education courses?

Some mortgage programs require first-time home buyers to take an educational course so they're informed and prepared for homeownership. For example, HomeReady by Fannie Mae and Home Possible by Freddie Mac both require first-time buyers to complete online education courses.

articles.title: Sarwar ministerial role sees promotion of another Starmer critic
articles.summary: Months after calling on Keir Starmer to quit, the Scottish Labour leader is set to become a minister in Burnham's government, the BBC's political editor writes.
articles.body:
The imminent appointment of the Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar to Andy Burnham's government, via a seat in the House of Lords, sees the promotion of another key figure in the downfall of Sir Keir Starmer as prime minister.

When Sarwar said publicly, back in February, that Sir Keir should stand down, it was a moment of colossal jeopardy for the now former prime minister.

It looked, briefly, like it might bring about an immediate and irrevocable collapse in his authority. Then, one after another, cabinet ministers posted their support for him on social media.

As I wrote at the time , missives of public loyalty from cabinet ministers towards a prime minister shouldn't be newsworthy and they only become so when the opposite seems feasible.

Now, five months on, Sarwar will be swapping Holyrood for Westminster and becoming a minister.

He will be joining Miatta Fahnbulleh in government, the new energy secretary in Burnham's cabinet, who was the first government minister to resign from Sir Keir's administration saying she had lost faith in him .

Also around the cabinet table, the new Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who let it be known in what turned out to be Sir Keir's final weeks in office that he had suggested to him that he ought to accept that his time was up.

It is also worth mentioning too John Healey, who resigned as defence secretary, and Wes Streeting, who resigned as health secretary towards the end of Sir Keir's time in Downing Street, are now in prominent roles in Burnham's cabinet as chancellor and defence secretary respectively.

This is the backdrop to comments from Steve Reed, the former communities secretary and doughty defender of Sir Keir at some of his moments of most intense peril.

Reed wrote to Burnham as he left government and said: "I hope those who did not show loyalty to Keir will now show it to you. I am proud that I acted with integrity at every step over the turbulent past few months."

There is, right now, as you would expect, overwhelming support for Burnham among Labour MPs.

But these public remarks from Reed are an indicator of the wells of private hurt and anger created by the events of recent days, weeks and months.

It is a reminder that, of course, all the folk you are reading and hearing about are human beings who have each keenly felt the tremors of uncertainty in recent months â and depending on their circumstances, outlook, instincts and judgement, have arrived at differing conclusions and decisions about how to act.

The public intervention of Darren Jones, another loyal lieutenant of the former prime minister, taking a swipe at the funding of the government's planned cut in VAT on domestic electricity bills should be seen in this context too.

Labour's switch from one leader to another was less drawn out and dramatic than it might have been, as there was neither a formal leadership challenge to Sir Keir, nor more than one contender to replace him once he had announced his intention to go.

But it is also true that what we have witnessed the climax of this week, and the build up to for months on end, is not cost or pain free for a political party and some of that is manifesting itself now â and may still do for some time.

articles.title: 'It can be isolating' - how does hot weather impact anxiety?
articles.summary: Southampton woman Lauren has health anxiety that gets worse during the hot weather.
articles.body:
"When it's hot the air feels different in your lungs. Your brain just starts going, 'Something's different - and therefore bad' even though it's not."

The hot weather and high temperatures can trigger anxiety and other mental health problems, according to new research from Oxford University.

Lauren Murphy, from Southampton, has anxiety and agoraphobia, a disorder defined by an intense fear of feeling trapped.

The heat can trigger this feeling of panic, making her feel "really isolated" and like she cannot breathe.

"You end up overthinking every single sensation, even if it's a regular everyday occurrence," she says.

The 34-year-old has had anxiety for about a decade, but noticed it became worse after she became a parent and was diagnosed with ADHD.

"When you're an anxious person, especially with health anxiety, you're so much more in tune with your body," she says.

Then her anxiety also got worse as the heat got stronger, which she first noticed when she went on holiday abroad a few years ago, and the high temperatures made her feel like she could not breathe.

When similar conditions arrived in the UK, she says those fears returned.

"It really brought it all back. This year has probably been the worst." she said.

A fourth heatwave of the year is affecting parts of the UK , with a drought declared across large parts of England and the whole of Wales.

"Your heart might be beating faster, you're sweating more, and all of that feels so alarming when you're anxious," Lauren says.

She says those physical sensations - including a heavy feeling in her chest, a racing heart and difficulty concentrating - can reinforce the symptoms of anxiety, creating a cycle that is difficult to break.

"It's like anxiety's the main character and you're the ensemble."

Lauren is not alone - a 2022 study from the University of Bath estimated that about 4.6% of people , external in the UK had climate anxiety.

It is a form of mental distress recognised by professional bodies and the NHS, with young people and women among the groups most at risk, according to a 2025 study , external .

"Heat stress might feel like anxiety, they have the same physiological response," says Professor Ciara MaCabe, who works at the University of Reading and specialises in mental health.

"So the anxiety feelings are due to the heat, and then anxiety can kick in.

"The more heatwaves we have obviously more and more people are going to experience this."

Lauren says she has since found ways to calm herself when she starts to panic.

"Journaling helps - your mind can think so much faster than you can write. Writing slows everything down," she says.

She says tapping techniques help "ground" her as well as breathing exercises, yoga and being in nature.

Her advice to others experiencing anxiety is to ask for help.

"I always underestimate my ability to cope," she says.

"Being brave isn't the absence of fear. It's having that fear and doing it anyway."

articles.title: In 2020, Minnesota funded a $1.918 million Shell Rock River habitat program; by 2025, it had protected or restored 588 acres
articles.summary: US News: In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. According to a 2025 final report.
articles.body: In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. According to a 2025 final report from the Lessard-Sams Outdoor Heritage Council, the program ultimately protected, restored or enhanced 588 acres of habitat in the Shell Rock River watershed, exceeding its original goal of 483 acres.A habitat program takes shapeThe funding was provided under Minnesota Laws 2020, with the appropriation directed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources for an agreement with the Shell Rock River Watershed District. The funding was intended to support land acquisition as well as the restoration and enhancement of aquatic habitat within the watershed. The program focused on several types of conservation work, including acquiring properties, restoring wetlands and improving aquatic habitat. The projects were selected using conservation planning and monitoring intended to identify areas where habitat improvements could provide significant benefits.The Shell Rock River Watershed is a shallow-lake system that supports fish, waterfowl and other wildlife. According to the final report, restoration projects were targeted at addressing habitat degradation and improving conditions for native fish, waterfowl and wildlife.Three properties protectedOne part of Phase IX involved acquiring three properties: the Glenville Property, the Bancroft Property, and the Church Lake Property. The District closed on the Glenville Property in March 2021 and the Bancroft Property in September 2021. For the Church Lake Property, the District transferred the deed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources in December 2024 after acquiring and restoring the parcel.The final report says these acquisitions contributed to the program's permanent protection of 218 acres. Another 370 acres of habitat and wetlands were enhanced or restored through the program. Together, those accomplishments contributed to the reported total of 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored.Wetlands and prairie restoredThe program included several restoration projects beyond property acquisition. The Bancroft Wetland Restoration was initiated in 2020, with construction beginning in June 2024 and largely completed by the fall of that year. Additional seeding work was completed in spring 2025. Another project focused on Panicum Prairie, where habitat enhancement work was carried out across 300 acres. The project involved native prairie vegetation and was substantially completed in February 2025, with final work completed in May.The program also supported the Fountain Lake In-Lake Habitat Project. Work included additional rock reefs and rock boulder clusters intended to improve fish habitat. The report notes that Phase IX funds were used to expand the scope of this work after the District determined additional funds were available. These projects addressed different parts of the watershed's ecosystem, from wetlands and prairie habitat to aquatic areas. The broader aim was to improve habitat conditions while protecting areas that could provide long-term benefits for wildlife.More acres than plannedThe program's original accomplishment plan called for 483 acres. By the end of the project, the final total had reached 588 acres, 105 acres more than initially planned. The report attributes the increase to the addition of the In-Lake Habitat Project and the Church Lake Property to Phase IX.According to the report, all grant funds were spent. The final grant expenditure remained $1.918 million, while the program's final total including leverage was $1.9479 million.A longer-term conservation effortThe work is intended to continue beyond the end of the grant. The Shell Rock River Watershed District relies on multiple funding sources, including a local option sales tax, local levy and public funding, to maintain conservation projects. The Minnesota Department of Natural Resources will also maintain the Church Lake Property, which it owns.The program's results illustrate how a single state-funded conservation effort can combine land protection, wetland restoration, prairie enhancement and aquatic habitat improvements. Rather than focusing on one habitat type, Phase IX combined several projects across the Shell Rock River watershed. By 2025, the program had moved beyond its original target, with the final report recording 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored. The completed work represents a combination of permanent land protection and habitat improvements designed to support Minnesota's fish, waterfowl and wildlife over the long term.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Quote of the day by King Charles: "To my darling Mama, as you begin your last great journey to join my dearâ¦" - a tribute to Queen Elizabeth, on gratitude, service and a son's farewell
articles.summary: UK News: Few words spoken at a moment of personal loss carry the weight of an entire lifetime. When Queen Elizabeth II died on 8 September 2022, her eldest son.
articles.body: Few words spoken at a moment of personal loss carry the weight of an entire lifetime. When Queen Elizabeth II died on 8 September 2022, her eldest son, King Charles III, addressed the nation the following day, speaking as both a new monarch and a grieving son at the same time. Recorded in the Blue Drawing Room at Buckingham Palace, with a framed portrait of his mother resting on the desk beside him, his tribute combined personal affection, real gratitude and a recognition of her extraordinary decades of public service. It became one of the most widely remembered moments of that entire period, quoted on front pages across the country the following morning. For millions watching, the address offered a rare glimpse behind the crown, where duty and private grief briefly occupied space. His carefully chosen words also captured the enormous responsibility that had suddenly passed to him, making the moment deeply personal and historically significant. The speech also reassured a grieving public that the values associated with Elizabethâs reign would continue, while Charles acknowledged the changes that lay ahead. His measured tone reflected both continuity and transition as Britain entered a new chapter.The address also marked the beginning of a new constitutional era, as Charles formally assumed the role his mother had held for seven decades. His message balanced continuity with change, reassuring the public while acknowledging the profound personal loss.Quote of the day by King Charles"To my darling Mama, as you begin your last great journey to join my dear late Papa, I want simply to say this: Thank you. Thank you for your love and devotion to our family and to the family of nations you have served so diligently all these years. May flights of angels sing thee to thy rest"What is the meaning of King Charles' quoteAt its heart, the message is about gratitude, love and farewell. Charles begins by describing his mother's death as a "last great journey," a gentle way of naming the end of a life, before referring directly to her reunion with her late husband, Prince Philip, who had died in April 2021. Rather than dwelling on the enormous constitutional change actually taking place, Charles places his mother's role firmly within a family context first. He thanks her for the love and devotion she gave to her family, before widening that same gratitude to the people and nations she served. The simplicity of the words "thank you," repeated before he expands on what he is actually grateful for, turns the tribute into an expression of appreciation for an entire lifetime of service.Why King Charles thanked Queen Elizabeth IIQueen Elizabeth II became monarch in 1952 and remained on the throne for more than seven decades, making her the longest-reigning monarch in British history. Across that period, she served under fifteen British prime ministers and witnessed enormous political, social and technological change. For Charles, though, her significance was never limited to her constitutional role alone. She was also, simply, his mother. His tribute moves between these two identities throughout, recognising her commitment to the "family of nations" she served while speaking about her in the deeply personal language of a son saying goodbye to his parent.The personal meaning behind "my darling Mama"The phrase "my darling Mama" gave the speech a genuinely intimate quality that stood apart from the formal language normally associated with royal addresses. Charles was speaking to a global audience, and yet the words themselves were directed towards one single person. Calling his mother "Mama" reflected the private family relationship sitting behind the public institution. Elizabeth II had been Queen to millions of people, but to her son she remained, simply, his mother. That contrast is really what gave the tribute its personal weight rather than letting it feel purely ceremonial.What "the family of nations" actually meansCharles' reference to the "family of nations" reflects Queen Elizabeth II's role across the Commonwealth, a voluntary association of independent countries, many with historical connections to the British Empire, of which she served as Head throughout her entire reign. Her role involved maintaining relationships with leaders and people across every member country, while representing a genuine continuity through decades of political change. Describing these countries as a "family of nations" highlighted exactly the relationships his mother had worked to maintain across the whole of her reign.Why Charles' farewell centred on serviceA central theme running through Queen Elizabeth II's public life was duty. In her 1952 accession broadcast, she pledged her life to the service of the people of the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth. Seven decades later, Charles' farewell returned directly to that same idea. Describing her as having served "so diligently all these years" recognised both the length and the sheer consistency of that commitment. It also reflected the unusual nature of her reign specifically, since she continued carrying out official duties well into her nineties, including appointing Liz Truss as prime minister only two days before her death.The Shakespeare reference at the end of the speechCharles closed his tribute with the words "May flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The line comes from William Shakespeare's Hamlet, Act 5, Scene 2, spoken by Horatio as he mourns his friend at the play's close, "Now cracks a noble heart. Good night, sweet prince, and flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The reference gave Charles' speech a genuinely literary and solemn conclusion, connecting his personal farewell to one of the most recognisable expressions of grief in English literature, and its suggestion of a peaceful passage into rest made it particularly fitting for a speech delivered the day after losing a parent.How the quote reflects the relationship between duty and familyOne of the most powerful aspects of Charles' tribute is how it brings together two sides of Queen Elizabeth II's life at once, a mother within her own family, and a monarch with responsibilities reaching far beyond it. Charles' words acknowledge both directly, first thanking her for her "love and devotion to our family," then expanding that same gratitude outward to the people and nations she served. In the same speech, he also announced that Prince William and Catherine would become the new Prince and Princess of Wales, and expressed his love for Harry and Meghan "as they continue to build their lives overseas," a reminder that even a historic constitutional address remained, underneath it, a message about family.How to apply the message in daily lifeThe circumstances behind this quote are genuinely unique, but its central message of gratitude applies just as well to ordinary relationships. Say thank you while you still can, since the people who matter most should never have to wait for a farewell to hear how much they are actually appreciated. Recognise quiet, unglamorous forms of service, since care and responsibility are often given without much recognition at all. Value family relationships alongside professional achievement, and remember that simple words of love and appreciation tend to become more meaningful, not less, with time.Some other memorable quotes by King Charles"I am a dangerous person because I mind about things.""It is important to be able to stand back and see the bigger picture.""The environment is something that is very close to my heart.""I think we have to be very careful about what we do to the natural world."Why King Charles' farewell remains memorableCharles' first address as King carried an unavoidable constitutional significance, and yet its most memorable passage was deeply personal. He was not simply acknowledging the end of a historic reign. He was saying goodbye to the woman who had been his mother for more than seven decades. The repeated "thank you" captures the central emotion of the entire tribute. After a lifetime defined by public duty, Charles chose to close his first address as monarch with something considerably more private, a reminder that behind every title and institution sits an ordinary human relationship. A queen can be a constitutional figure to an entire nation while remaining, simply, "Mama" to her own son.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

That contrast is really what gave the tribute its personal weight rather than letting it feel purely ceremonial.What "the family of nations" actually meansCharles' reference to the "family of nations" reflects Queen Elizabeth II's role across the Commonwealth, a voluntary association of independent countries, many with historical connections to the British Empire, of which she served as Head throughout her entire reign. Her role involved maintaining relationships with leaders and people across every member country, while representing a genuine continuity through decades of political change. Describing these countries as a "family of nations" highlighted exactly the relationships his mother had worked to maintain across the whole of her reign.Why Charles' farewell centred on serviceA central theme running through Queen Elizabeth II's public life was duty. In her 1952 accession broadcast, she pledged her life to the service of the people of the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth. Seven decades later, Charles' farewell returned directly to that same idea. Describing her as having served "so diligently all these years" recognised both the length and the sheer consistency of that commitment. It also reflected the unusual nature of her reign specifically, since she continued carrying out official duties well into her nineties, including appointing Liz Truss as prime minister only two days before her death.The Shakespeare reference at the end of the speechCharles closed his tribute with the words "May flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The line comes from William Shakespeare's Hamlet, Act 5, Scene 2, spoken by Horatio as he mourns his friend at the play's close, "Now cracks a noble heart. Good night, sweet prince, and flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The reference gave Charles' speech a genuinely literary and solemn conclusion, connecting his personal farewell to one of the most recognisable expressions of grief in English literature, and its suggestion of a peaceful passage into rest made it particularly fitting for a speech delivered the day after losing a parent.How the quote reflects the relationship between duty and familyOne of the most powerful aspects of Charles' tribute is how it brings together two sides of Queen Elizabeth II's life at once, a mother within her own family, and a monarch with responsibilities reaching far beyond it. Charles' words acknowledge both directly, first thanking her for her "love and devotion to our family," then expanding that same gratitude outward to the people and nations she served. In the same speech, he also announced that Prince William and Catherine would become the new Prince and Princess of Wales, and expressed his love for Harry and Meghan "as they continue to build their lives overseas," a reminder that even a historic constitutional address remained, underneath it, a message about family.How to apply the message in daily lifeThe circumstances behind this quote are genuinely unique, but its central message of gratitude applies just as well to ordinary relationships. Say thank you while you still can, since the people who matter most should never have to wait for a farewell to hear how much they are actually appreciated. Recognise quiet, unglamorous forms of service, since care and responsibility are often given without much recognition at all. Value family relationships alongside professional achievement, and remember that simple words of love and appreciation tend to become more meaningful, not less, with time.Some other memorable quotes by King Charles"I am a dangerous person because I mind about things.""It is important to be able to stand back and see the bigger picture.""The environment is something that is very close to my heart.""I think we have to be very careful about what we do to the natural world."Why King Charles' farewell remains memorableCharles' first address as King carried an unavoidable constitutional significance, and yet its most memorable passage was deeply personal. He was not simply acknowledging the end of a historic reign. He was saying goodbye to the woman who had been his mother for more than seven decades. The repeated "thank you" captures the central emotion of the entire tribute. After a lifetime defined by public duty, Charles chose to close his first address as monarch with something considerably more private, a reminder that behind every title and institution sits an ordinary human relationship. A queen can be a constitutional figure to an entire nation while remaining, simply, "Mama" to her own son.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Who voted for Count Binface in the Clacton by-election and why?
articles.summary: Cheaper Flakes and using Adele to fund the NHS - voters on why they support a man dressed as a bin.
articles.body:
Self-styled intergalactic space warrior Count Binface finished second in the Clacton by-election on Thursday with 9,455 votes.

A record 34 candidates stood in the contest, but Binface and Reform UK leader Nigel Farage were the only contenders to secure more than 500 votes.

The other major UK parties boycotted the election, which was triggered by Farage's resignation as an MP in July, having won the seat from the Conservatives in 2024.

Binface has stood in various high-profile elections around the country in recent years. Before Clacton, his best results were more than 24,000 votes in the last two London mayoral elections.

With more candidates on the ballot than ever before, why did 26.9% of voters choose a man wearing a bin on his head?

First-time voter Ben Peters, 18, from Holland-on-Sea, said the election had been a "joke" since the start.

He said: "It was a bit of a thrill, but at the same time it felt almost pointless because I knew that, no matter what I did, Farage was going to get back into the seat."

Stephen Bear jailed over sex offender breaches

Has the by-election changed things for Clacton?

Anti-asylum protester who shoved police is jailed

Binface's policies had included nationalising the singer Adele, moving a pub hand dryer in Uxbridge and enforcing a 99p price tag on ice creams with 99 flakes.

Peters said: "Even if it means voting for Count Binface and getting 99p ice creams for 99 flakes, that is one more step than Nigel Farage has ever done for Clacton."

Alex Greenwood, from Thorpe-le-Soken, acknowledged some policies were "a bit silly" but the 18-year-old student argued there was an underlying logic to them.

"Nationalising Adele... all of Adele's song proceeds go to a private company which goes to shareholders and her songs are pretty much cultural icons," he said.

"It's not actually that far-fetched... why not have all that money go to the government which could be used on the NHS and stuff?"

Greenwood suggested his vote was partially a protest against Farage, whom he believes called the by-election to avoid scrutiny from the Office of the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards .

He added: "I do like Binface. I don't like Farage all that much."

Before Farage quit his Clacton seat in July, Parliament's standards watchdog had been investigating him for not declaring a Â£5m gift he received from billionaire Reform UK donor Christopher Harborne before he became an MP.

He said the by-election was a "people versus the establishment" showdown, saying the "people of Clacton should be the judges of my actions".

Kerry Mitchell, who lives in Wix, said she had voted for Count Binface because he would have made for a "more credible, honest, responsible, not to say committed, MP than Nigel Farage".

The 61-year-old, who voted Labour in 2024, said: "Nigel Farage poses a real threat to democracy in the UK and if Binface had won, it would have put an end to him.

"And it also added some much-needed humour and lightness into politics.

"The world is in a very dark place at the moment, and a bit of levity and humour is fantastic, especially when you contrast it with the rhetoric of outrage, division and anger that we hear from the far-right."

Tracey Donovan, 61, also voted Labour in the last general election and decided to back Binface on Thursday because it was "the only viable alternative to Farage".

"I detest Farage and everything he stands for. He has done absolutely nothing for our constituency," she told the BBC.

"I want an MP who represents our area with the constituents' interests being addressed.

"He claims the establishment is against him, but he is the establishment."

Donovan, who has lived in Clacton her entire life, added she was pleasantly surprised by how many people voted for Binface.

"He had almost a third of the votes cast as supposedly a joke candidate, and I'm very pleased that it is only really just over a quarter of the constituency [voting] population who actively backed Farage and Reform," she said.

"Count Binface could have rid this town of its Little Britain label if more of the 55% who didn't vote at all had got out there and voted against Farage."

Salon owner Verda Rigby, who lives in St Osyth, used to vote for the Conservatives before she "became a socialist" and started supporting Labour.

In this election, however, as voting for Labour was not an option, the 66-year-old instead opted for Binface.

"I could have stayed at home, but we fought for the right to vote and, look, it was partly for the joke that Farage is," she said.

"And I despise the right-wing parties Reform, Restore, and Reclaim - it's like a bad pop group of numpties."

People in Clacton react to Nigel Farage's re-election

Philip Bird, 66, has lived in Clacton for 30 years and said he, too, would have voted for Labour if the party had stood a candidate in the election.

"I think it was absolutely right not to stand anyone because none of the major parties should have condoned this election," he said.

"It was farcical, completely unnecessary, and designed to distract attention, and it wasn't going to change anything, so I was quite comfortable voting for a satirical candidate.

"Farage has greatly harmed the conversation in this country, he has been a dreadful MP, he has done nothing for Clacton, and in reality his politics are precisely what Clacton doesn't need."

In a statement after his win on Friday , the Reform leader said: "The verdict is now in, and it is a convincing, overwhelming win, with more votes than we got in the general election of 2024.

"Today, the voters in Clacton have stuck up two fingers to the entire political establishment."

articles.title: Children's stunted lungs show recovery in ultra low emission zone
articles.summary: Children's lung capacity caught up with their peers in less polluted areas once a clean air zone came in, a study shows.
articles.body:
Scientists say they have been "stunned" by how quickly young children's lungs began to recover and grow after pollution restrictions were brought in where they lived.

Researchers found that children in London whose lung growth had been stunted by pollution showed impressive improvements after the introduction of an Ultra Low Emission Zone (Ulez) in 2019 reduced emissions.

The study followed more than 3,400 primary school children in London and Luton and provides what scientists believe is the strongest evidence yet that local clean air zones could help reduce some of the harm caused by pollution during childhood.

But independent researchers caution that other factors must also be considered.

Air pollution can stunt the growth of young children's lungs leaving them at an increased risk of asthma, heart disease, diabetes and even premature death.

Children are also more vulnerable to pollution because their lungs and immune systems are still developing. And when outside, they tend to be closer to the ground and nearer sources of exhaust fumes, for example.

In 2020 Ella Adoo-Kissi-Debrah, a nine-year-old girl from London who died following an asthma attack in 2013, became the first person in the UK to have air pollution listed as a cause of death .

In the study, researchers recruited six to nine-year-olds attending primary schools in London's ultra low emission zone and followed the same children for five years, comparing them to similar children (in terms of socio-economic background, physical activity and ethnicity) in Luton.

Children in the study had annual lung function and capacity tests in the year before Ulez came in and for four years after.

Initial results showed children's lungs in London were smaller in capacity than those in Luton, which is less polluted than London but has a similar mix of pollutants.

At the end of the study the children's lung capacity reached near identical levels in both groups.

"While we would expect children's lungs to grow year on year, our results indicate that the London children's lung growth had accelerated during the four years to 'catch up' with the control group in Luton to reach similar levels of lung capacity," researchers say.

"I was absolutely stunned when I first saw the results," Prof Chris Griffiths, a senior author on the study, at Queen Mary University of London, told the BBC.

"The speed of catch up in lung capacity in the London group was surprising and impressive.

"This shows an ambitious clean air zone can drive pollution levels down, rapidly restoring children's stunted lung growth."

The main test measured how much air a child could forcibly breathe out in one second after a big breath in.

In practical terms the improvements could mean children in the London group could run as fast as the Luton group without getting out of breath or blow out the same number of candles for example, Griffiths explained.

Another way of testing for lung capacity used in the study showed significant improvements too, though not to the same extent - implying there are still gains to be made.

Overall the proportion of children in London whose lung capacity was deemed "clinically impaired" (suggesting lung damage resulting in coughs or breathlessness) fell from 14% to 9%.

In Luton - where some smaller scale measures were put in place to tackle air pollution - the figures were 9% to 7%.

The team's measurements also showed the level of nitrogen dioxide children were exposed to fell faster in London than in Luton over this time.

Researchers say this is key as it likely demonstrates that the improved lung growth they saw was related to air quality improvements following the implementation of Ulez.

London's Ulez was first introduced in 2019 by Mayor Sadiq Khan in a bid to "clean up London's air". London had high levels of the harmful gas nitrogen dioxide which comes from motor vehicles.

Older, more polluting vehicles had to pay a daily charge to drive in central London. The measures were later expanded to cover the whole capital. While many supported the policy it provoked political opposition and protests.

Prof Anna Hansell, at the University of Leicester, who was not involved in the study said the improved lung function in children was "likely to have lifelong benefits for their health."

She added the study was "carefully conducted by "well-respected researchers" and that the geographical comparisons between London and Luton were important as there had been general reductions in air pollution over time.

"This proved particularly useful, given that the study period included the Covid-19 pandemic â and demonstrates the findings in London are not due to changes related to the pandemic," she said.

Another aspect to consider was that the London group may have been more likely to walk or cycle to school once Ulez came in.

Meanwhile, Kevin McConway, emeritus professor at the Open University, said it was important to take the full impact of Covid into account and argued that studying other cities could help tease out whether some improvements were due to unmeasured differences between London and Luton.

Lead author, Dr Helen Wood, at Queen Mary University of London said while the results were very promising there was no room for complacency as "air pollution in both London and Luton â as well as other cities across the UK â remains above WHO guideline levels, so there is still work to be done".

"We know clean air zones are a complex area and the impact on businesses and individuals must be considered. What we are doing is adding new evidence to inform the debate," Griffiths said.

"There are more than a billion kids living in cities around the world, most of them in polluted environments, getting a really bad start in life.

"That's why these are important findings with global relevance."

The work involved researchers from the Universities of Bedfordshire, Oxford, Cambridge, Edinburgh and Southern California and is published in the Lancet Public Health , external .

Update 20 August: A link to the study was added to this article.

articles.title: Coroner positively identifies human remains as those of LaShaunda Spurlock, a South Carolina woman who vanished two years ago
articles.summary: The Marlboro County Coroner’s Office has positively identified human remains found in Bennettsville, South Carolina, in April as those of missing woman LaShaunda Spurlock.
articles.body: It’s been nearly four months since human remains were discovered in Bennettsville, ​​South Carolina. On April 23, the Bennettsville Police Department shared a news release on Facebook saying officers were “actively investigating the discovery of human remains found within a trash receptacle at a local housing apartment.” Police responded to the scene after receiving a report of “suspicious contents inside a trash can.” Four days later, authorities announced they had arrested Luke Douglas Jr., who they “believed to be the last person to have seen” the victim. At the time, the person’s identity had not been positively determined. In announcing the arrest, police said Douglas had “provided information and evidence that led to a confession” in which he “admitted to concealing the victim’s remains by placing the decomposing body in a storage area within the apartment where he resided” before disposing of them. Now, the Chesterfield County Sheriff’s Office has shared an update in the investigation. The office said the Marlboro County Coroner’s Office had positively identified the remains. “The Marlboro County Coroner’s Office has confirmed that the remains have been positively identified as LaShaunda Spurlock, 43, of Chesterfield County,” the sheriff’s office wrote. LaShaunda was last seen outside her home in Society Hill in April 2024. “Dateline” featured her disappearance in its Missing in America digital series in November of that year. Her sister, Tabitha Caudell, told “Dateline” at the time that a neighbor saw LaShaunda getting into a car on April 29. “A neighbor reported seeing her getting into a red older model vehicle, possibly a Kia Soul, on that day around 5:00 to 6:00 p.m. with two men,” Tabitha said. “She hasn’t been seen since.” “For nearly two years, the Spurlock family has lived with uncertainty while holding onto hope and searching for answers,” the Chesterfield County Sheriff’s Office said on Facebook this week. “While this confirmation provides an answer to one of the many questions surrounding LaShaunda’s disappearance, we know this news also brings unimaginable heartbreak to those who love her.” Douglas has been charged with destruction, desecration or removal of human remains and destroying, altering, concealing or tampering with physical evidence or biological material, according to the Marlboro County court website. He has not yet appeared in court. “Dateline” reached out to Douglas’ attorney for comment but has not yet heard back. If you have a story to share with Dateline, please submit it here.

articles.title: John Swinney defends Â£45,000 business-class flights to World Cup
articles.summary: The Scottish government spent almost Â£100,000 on official visits to the United States in June.
articles.body:
John Swinney has defended the use of more than Â£45,000 of public funds on business-class flights for him and two senior aides to the World Cup.

Scotland's first minister flew to Boston on 11 June for Scotland's opening match, before taking part in trade talks in Kentucky three days later.

While he and two senior officials travelled business class, Sports Minister Maree Todd and several other officials went to the US on significantly cheaper economy-class flights.

Swinney insisted the government had sought to "minimise" costs, while Justice Secretary Neil Gray defended the business class flights as a means of ensuring ministers "arrive fresh" when they travel overseas.

In total, the government spent Â£98,442 on trips for Swinney, Todd and their officials to the US, including flights, hotels and expenses.

Flights for Swinney and his private secretary John Webster cost Â£17,893 each.

Business-class tickets for the first minister's special adviser Colin McAllister cost Â£9,864.

articles.title: Imran Khan's kin say Pak govt violated court order for not taking ex-PM to private hospital
articles.summary: Pakistan News: NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan was shifted back to Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi early Friday, hours after he was taken for a medical examinatio.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan was shifted back to Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi early Friday, hours after he was taken for a medical examination amid a legal battle over his health and demands from his family and supporters for better medical care.Khan, 73, was taken to the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad, Pakistan's information minister Attaullah Tarar said, news agaency PTI reports. The government later said Khan was medically fit and returned him to jail at around 5 am.The development came days after the Supreme Court ordered authorities to move Khan to Al-Shifa hospital following a medical report that said he was suffering from âlevel three plusâ anxiety.Family alleges violation of court orderKhan's family has repeatedly raised concerns about his access to adequate medical treatment while in custody. His sister, Uzma Khan, was present during the medical examination at PIMS, according to AP. They have accused authorities of violating a court order by taking him to a government hospital for a medical examination instead of a private hospital designated by the court.She alleged that during their meeting, Khan complained of being kept in solitary confinement, which she described as âmental tortureâ for the former prime minister.Khanâs personal physician, Faisal Sultan, said he had been taken to Shifa International Hospital, where he waited for Khan until early Friday. He was later informed that Khan had instead been returned to Adiala prison in Rawalpindi.Tarar said authorities changed the plan because of security concerns after supporters of Khanâs Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) gathered outside Shifa International Hospital or were heading there.Khan has been in custody since his arrest on August 5, 2023, in a corruption case.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Make a Difference Awards NI: Belfast 'hidden gem' among finalists
articles.summary: Annadale Community Garden Group is one of four groups or individuals in the running for this year's Make a Difference Awards NI.
articles.body:
From a lifeless strip of grass to a blossoming garden, Annadale Community Centre's grounds have received a glow up over the past year, becoming a "hidden gem" for all to enjoy.

The volunteer group has now been recognised for its contribution to the local area, receiving a nomination for the BBC Make a Difference Awards .

Annadale Community Centre Gardening Group meets every Tuesday and will celebrate its first birthday in September.

Residents say the space has not only improved the local environment but has also created a welcoming community hub where people can learn new skills, share ideas and support each other through life's challenges.

Kirstie Rowan has been involved since the beginning and is proud of the journey the group has been on, which has been full of "lovely big changes".

"We started with the grass, unwanted containers and the polytunnel and now we have all of this â we've got the pond, tree bed and vegetables as well," she explained.

"Every week when we come down there's always more growth, more flowers, new flowers, it really is beautiful.

"Some of us don't work so this gets us out of the house weekly and even if we come, we aren't expected to do anything, its just nice to be here with everyone."

For Fayth Duffy, being part of the group has been a "game changer" for her after recently moving to the area.

"I was really finding it hard to put down roots and meet friends because when your kids get a bit older you're not meeting the mums at the gate, you're not getting out to the other places such as toddler groups," she said.

"We've all become such good friends, we go for coffee together sometimes afterwards and support each other, we'll ring each other to make sure we are all here."

For local resident Larry Andrews the group has been a refuge following the death of his wife last year.

"I came here for a bit of company, my daughter found it on WhatsApp and I've been coming since September last year," he said.

The 87-year-old former butcher has made new friends through the group.

"It's good to meet different people and have a yarn with themâ¦ It's amazing the number of people you do find," he added.

Amber Jennings works with the group and is on hand with gardening tips and advice.

"It means a lot to be nominated for this award - I feel like this is such a hidden gem on the Ormeau Road for people to retreat to on a Tuesday morning and learn how to garden with those in the community," she said.

The primary goal of the group is to "improve the wellbeing of people in the area".

Jennings has seen first hand the difference the garden has made to members.

"It's been a really uplifting experience for all involved, having that routine, knowing you're outside and being with people in your community," she added.

It is awarded to an individual or group who improve or conserve their local environment.

Annadale Community Centre Garden Group is one of four finalists in the category, along with:

Daniel McAfee - Ballycastle, a wildlife volunteer and member of the Glens Red Squirrel Group where he shares his knowledge through school visits, talks and guided nature walks

Alannah Agnew - Cookstown , a passionate member and chairperson of her school eco team. She has led assemblies on climate change, littering and healthy eating, while helping her school achieve its sixth Green Flag award

Eco Rangers NI - Carrickfergus, a community litter-picking group that clears litter year-round, supports community events and helps young people with awards such as the Duke of Edinburgh Award

Overall winners will be announced live on Vinny and Cate's BBC Radio Ulster show on Friday 25 September.
